coordinateSource.label: U.S. Maritime Administration — Black Point, 5 May 1945 torpedoing and historical incident coordinates

metadataReview.note: The U.S. Maritime Administration records the 5 May 1945 torpedoing of Black Point by U-853 at this historical incident position. This opening attack provides a documented anchor for the Battle of Point Judith of 5–6 May. The subsequent antisubmarine search and attacks extended south toward Block Island; this point does not locate the final U-853 wreck, every attack, or the entire engagement. Dates and unquantified forces are unchanged.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: MARAD historical incident coordinates for the torpedoing of Black Point: 41°19′02″ N, 71°25′01″ W, converted arithmetically to longitude first and rounded to six decimals. The source classifies its location accuracy as “Historic 1” without a metric error radius. This is the opening attack location, not a surveyed battle center or the U-853 wreck position; the later pursuit covered other waters.
